model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Used observed timing only to frame the hypothesis; the controller must run full correctness and official timing before drawing conclusions.

memory_lessons.applicability: The observed configurations use the same 128-thread CTA and compact source representation, making tile size a relevant factor for this experiment; do not assume an intermediate size interpolates in performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The 128-source configuration measured 0.0008998 s and the 256-source configuration measured 0.0011024 s; both were correct. These observations motivate testing an intermediate tile size but do not predict its result.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare the official timing for the 192-source tile against both prior configurations, using the same correctness suite and timing protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: With the 128-thread CTA and target mapping unchanged, a 192-source tile may balance the lower shared-memory footprint of a 128-source tile against fewer tile iterations than a 256-source tile. The prior timings favor the 128-source configuration, so this intermediate size is a testable tradeoff, not an assumed speedup.

retained: Use a 192-entry compact shared-memory source tile with the existing 128-thread CTA and 128-target launch mapping.
Set dynamic shared memory to 3072 bytes, matching 192 compact entries of four floats each.

Retain cooperative bounded loads, both CTA barriers per tile, partial-tile handling, self-interaction exclusion by global index, one accumulator and output per target thread, and unchanged integration.
